decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's consumer-health, pharmacy, and supplement know-how, this range fits existing capabilities and can be supported without stretching absorptive capacity.
This skin and hair supplement builds directly on the firm's established supplement and OTC knowledge base, so management is likely to keep learning from it rather than exit quickly.
A joint-health supplement is closely related to the firm's existing consumer-health offer and pharmacy channels, making continued commercialization and incremental improvement plausible.
Although somewhat more novel in concept, this immune supplement still sits near the firm's established supplement portfolio and can be refined using its formulation, quality, and market knowledge.

Because this product is more distant from the firm's established knowledge base and already showed a serious market problem, management is likely to reallocate resources to areas where it can learn and control quality more effectively.

Despite being more distant, this OTC migraine product still leverages the firm's pharmaceutical development, regulatory, and pharmacy-channel capabilities, so management would likely give it more time before withdrawing it.
